headline: On 6 two-story git batches (2 repetitions, Haiku 5.5 xhigh, Jev live) plain Haiku and Haiku with the round-2 verifier both pass 10 of 12 runs; c6 is wrong in both arms because its gold (S2 PASS) is inherited from the tool's own fixture, whose AC-coverage row cites a test that is on no branch. Tokens 7.54M -> 7.56M (+0.2%; round 1 was +28%), inside the repetition noise, with no case worse; the report still did not replace the agents' own merge and test runs. Top fix: rebuild the cases as harder multi-fault batches with a corrected c6 gold.

arms.name: Plain Claude (inspects manifests, logs and branches itself; verify-batch.mjs prints "verifier disabled")
arms.model: haiku (claude-haiku-5-5), forced by the user; the router would have said sonnet/opus

arms.name: Claude + integration-verifier round 2 (verify-batch.mjs runs verifyBatch with --jev and prints the verdict-first report)
arms.model: haiku (claude-haiku-5-5), forced by the user; the router would have said sonnet/opus
arms.engineVersion: typesafe/jev-1.13 via OpenRouter decisions API, shadow only (statuses never change)

evaluation.planVersion: design.md (frozen before measurement; same cases, gold, prompts and arms as round 1; only the tool changed)
evaluation.datasetVersion: fixtures c1-c6 built by make_tasks.mjs (unchanged from round 1); gold unchanged, written by hand before round 1
evaluation.tokenScope: all tokens of each case agent's session (input + output + cache read + cache write), from its subagent transcript
deviations: Steps 1-3 (brainstorm, Gate A, implementation) were skipped on the user's instruction: retro round 2 of an existing tool. The two round-1 suggestions were implemented by an Opus subagent on branch claude/integration-verifier-round2 (commit b7883e5), reviewed by a fresh Opus reviewer.

Independent review of round 2 (opus): 0 Critical, 0 Major new. Four Minor and one Suggestion stay open (agent-review.json): a bad covered row is silently ignored when the AC has other evidence; cat-file accepts a directory; verdict lines join in a Markdown viewer; git stderr can add newlines. Round-1 Majors (self-written evidence, log_path, Windows timeouts, Jev redaction) are carried over and accepted by the user for this run, not fixed.

c6 gold is inherited and kept for a paired comparison: S2 gold PASS, but the tool and both arms answer REVIEW_REQUIRED because the cited test tests/count.test.js is on no branch. c6 is wrong in both arms in all four runs. The tool's new behaviour agrees with the agents; the gold is the flaw. Not a tool win or loss.

Contamination: a c2 rep-1 B agent ran git checkout in this worktree instead of the batch repo, moving it to a stray branch for a while. Three B runs that started in that window (c1.B.r1, c2.B.r1, c3.B.r1) ran the pre-round-2 verify.mjs (c1 and c3 confirmed by their old report format); c2.B.r2 never ran the tool to completion. All four were discarded (evidence/contaminated-run1/) and re-run in fresh folders c<n>.B2.r<n> with the same prompt and fixtures; aliases.json maps them. Worktree restored to claude/integration-verifier-round2, stray branch deleted.
Arm A contamination check: 0 forbidden calls (integration-verifier, verify.mjs, gold, logs, B folders, private folder) in all 12 arm-A transcripts; no A case re-run.

Measurement collection: collect.mjs was changed to take the first line starting with BATCH: as the B output (round 1 matched the old header, which a source-file read can also contain). A texts are the first tool result of each arm-A agent (usually a folder listing), since arm A never runs the wrapper.
Jev was live but called only in c5 (1 call per run, 2 in total, label code_regression, 763 and 819 ms); it never changed a status.
All case agents ran on Haiku 5.5 with effort xhigh by the user's decision; the reviewers ran on opus. At most 6 case agents in flight; A and B of a case launched together (repetition 2: B first).

Case set is too easy to separate the arms: 5 of 6 cases are the tool's own fixtures, plain Haiku gets all but the flawed c6 right in both arms, and the prompt gives arm A the tool's status rules. Two-story batches; directional only.

Per-case token gaps (B vs A, mean of 2 reps): c1 +3%, c2 +18%, c3 -33%, c4 -13%, c5 +12%, c6 +18%; repetitions within one case differ by up to 2x (c3 B 565k vs 360k), so no per-case difference is established.
